stem: Heat is a form of __________ that flows from a hotter body to a colder body.
solution: Heat is a form of energy that flows from a hotter body to a colder one.

stem: The degree of hotness or coldness of a body is measured by its __________.
solution: Temperature is the measure of the hotness or coldness of a body.

stem: The instrument used to measure temperature is a __________.
solution: A thermometer measures temperature.

stem: Heat flows from a body at __________ temperature to one at __________ temperature.
solution: Heat flows spontaneously from a hotter (higher-temperature) body to a colder one.

stem: The transfer of heat through a solid without the material itself moving is called __________.
solution: In conduction, heat passes through a material from particle to particle without bulk movement.

stem: The transfer of heat in liquids and gases by the actual movement of the heated material is called __________.
solution: Convection transfers heat in fluids as warmer parts rise and cooler parts sink.

stem: The transfer of heat without any medium, as from the Sun to the Earth, is called __________.
solution: Radiation transfers heat as electromagnetic waves and needs no medium.

stem: Materials that allow heat to pass through easily are called __________.
solution: Good conductors, like metals, allow heat to pass through easily.

stem: Materials that do not allow heat to pass through easily are called __________.
solution: Insulators such as wood, plastic and air are poor conductors of heat.

stem: Which of the following is the best conductor of heat?
solution: Metals like copper are excellent conductors of heat; wood, plastic and air are insulators.

stem: The handles of cooking utensils are made of wood or plastic because these are __________.
solution: Insulating handles do not let heat reach the hand, preventing burns.

stem: The heat from the Sun reaches the Earth mainly by __________.
solution: The Sun's heat crosses the vacuum of space by radiation.

stem: Sea breeze and land breeze are examples of heat transfer by __________.
solution: Sea and land breezes are convection currents caused by uneven heating of land and water.

stem: During the day, a sea breeze blows from the sea to the land because __________.
options: land heats up faster, and cooler air from the sea flows in
solution: Land heats faster during the day; warm air over land rises and cooler air from the sea flows in as a sea breeze.

stem: At night, a land breeze blows __________.
solution: At night the sea stays warmer; warm air over the sea rises and cooler air from land flows out — a land breeze.

stem: Dark-coloured surfaces are __________ absorbers of heat than light-coloured surfaces.
solution: Dark surfaces absorb more heat (and radiate more) than light-coloured surfaces.

stem: We prefer light-coloured clothes in summer because they __________.
options: reflect most of the heat and keep us cooler
solution: Light colours reflect much of the Sun's heat, keeping us cooler in summer.

stem: We prefer dark-coloured clothes in winter because they __________.
options: absorb more heat and keep us warmer
solution: Dark colours absorb more heat, helping keep us warmer in winter.

stem: Most substances __________ on heating and __________ on cooling.
solution: Substances generally expand when heated and contract when cooled.

stem: A gap is left between railway rails to allow for __________ in hot weather.
solution: Rails expand in heat; the gaps prevent the track from bending due to thermal expansion.

stem: Woollen clothes keep us warm in winter mainly because __________.
options: wool traps air, a poor conductor of heat
solution: Wool traps air, an insulator, reducing heat loss from the body.

stem: Wearing several thin layers of clothes is warmer than one thick layer because __________.
options: air trapped between layers acts as an insulator
solution: Air trapped between clothing layers is a good insulator, reducing heat loss.

stem: In a room, a heater warms the whole room mainly by __________.
solution: Warm air rises and cooler air sinks, setting up convection currents that spread heat.

stem: Radiation of heat can travel through __________.
solution: Radiation needs no medium and can travel through vacuum, as sunlight reaches Earth.

stem: A cold metal spoon in hot tea becomes warm at the top because of __________.
solution: Heat travels along the metal spoon by conduction, warming the far end.

stem: A sweater does not give us heat; it only __________.
options: reduces the loss of body heat
solution: A sweater is an insulator that slows the escape of body heat; it does not generate heat.

stem: Which of the following correctly matches a mode of heat transfer with an example?
options: Convection – heat through a metal rod
Radiation – warming a spoon in tea
solution: Radiation carries the Sun's heat to Earth. (Sea breeze is convection; a metal rod/spoon warming is conduction.)

stem: A metal chair left in the Sun feels hotter than a wooden chair because metal __________.
options: conducts heat to the hand faster
is at a higher temperature always
solution: Metal conducts heat to (and from) the hand quickly, so it feels hotter in the Sun and colder in the cold.

stem: Hot air balloons rise because the heated air inside is __________ than the surrounding air.
solution: Heating makes the air inside expand and become less dense, so the balloon rises — a convection effect.

stem: A vacuum (thermos) flask keeps drinks hot or cold by minimizing heat transfer through __________.
solution: A vacuum flask reduces all three: vacuum stops conduction/convection, and shiny walls reduce radiation.

stem: The shiny, silvered walls of a thermos flask reduce heat loss by __________.
solution: Silvered surfaces reflect heat radiation, reducing heat transfer by radiation.

stem: Ventilators are placed near the ceiling of a room because __________.
options: warm, used air rises and escapes through them
solution: Warm air rises by convection and escapes through high ventilators, letting fresh air enter below.

stem: The normal temperature of the human body is about __________.
solution: Normal human body temperature is about 37 °C.

stem: The temperature at which pure water boils at normal pressure is __________.
solution: Water boils at 100 °C at normal atmospheric pressure.

stem: The temperature at which pure water freezes is __________.
solution: Pure water freezes at 0 °C at normal pressure.

stem: Convection currents cannot be set up in __________.
solution: Convection needs the material to move freely, so it occurs in fluids, not in rigid solids.

stem: Which of the following will feel hotter after being left in the Sun for the same time?
solution: The black surface absorbs the most heat, so it feels hottest.

stem: The winds and ocean currents on the Earth are driven mainly by __________.
options: uneven heating of the Earth by the Sun (convection)
solution: Uneven solar heating sets up convection in the air and oceans, driving winds and currents.

stem: A thermometer works because the liquid inside it __________ on heating.
solution: The thermometric liquid expands on heating, rising up the tube to indicate temperature.

stem: Cooking pots are made of metal because metals are __________.
solution: Metals conduct heat well, so cooking pots are made of metal.

stem: Which statement about heat and temperature is correct?
options: Heat is energy in transit; temperature measures hotness
Heat and temperature are the same
solution: Heat is the energy that flows due to a temperature difference; temperature measures the degree of hotness.

stem: A land–sea breeze is an example of heat transfer that occurs in __________.
solution: Land and sea breezes are convection currents in the atmosphere (a gas).

stem: The reason a black car heats up faster than a white car in sunlight is that black __________.
solution: Black surfaces absorb more heat radiation, so a black car heats up faster.

stem: Which of the following is an insulator used to reduce heat loss?
solution: Thermocol and other foams are insulators used to reduce heat loss; metals conduct heat.

stem: Meteors burn up on entering the atmosphere due to heat produced by __________.
solution: Friction with air molecules heats meteors so much that they burn up.

stem: The transfer of heat in the boiling of water in a pot occurs mainly by __________.
solution: In boiling water, hot water rises and cool water sinks, setting up convection currents.

stem: Igloos (snow houses) keep the inside warm because __________.
options: snow traps air and is a poor conductor of heat
solution: Snow traps air (an insulator), reducing heat loss and keeping the inside of an igloo relatively warm.

stem: The main reason we feel warm sitting near a fire is __________.
options: heat radiated from the fire reaches us
solution: The fire's heat reaches us mainly by radiation, warming us without contact.

stem: A thermos (vacuum) flask keeps drinks hot or cold by minimising heat transfer through __________.
solution: The vacuum stops conduction and convection, and the shiny walls reduce radiation, so the flask keeps contents hot or cold.

stem: During the day at the seashore, cool air blows from the sea to the land as a __________.
solution: By day, land heats faster than the sea; the warm air over land rises and cool air blows in from the sea as the sea breeze.

stem: The overall message of the chapter 'Heat Transfer in Nature' is that:
options: heat flows from hot to cold by conduction, convection and radiation, explaining natural phenomena like winds and breezes and guiding our use of conductors and insulators
heat and temperature are the same
heat flows from cold to hot
heat has no modes of transfer
solution: The chapter explains heat transfer by conduction, convection and radiation, natural phenomena like breezes, and the use of conductors and insulators.
